title: Poland Minimum Wage 2026: Tax, Pension Age and Energy Prices Compared
content:
Updated 25 October 2026

Quick answer: In Poland in 2026, the minimum wage is €1,119/month (about $1,252 a month full time); an average earner keeps 76% of their pay after income tax and social security; household electricity costs €0.300 per kWh; petrol is €1.56/L, up 13.3% since February; the state pension age is 65 men / 60 women. The table below puts 8 everyday money measures for Poland side by side and ranks each one against the other countries in our data, using official figures from national statistics offices, central banks, the OECD and Eurostat.

Most comparisons of Poland look at one number at a time. This page gathers the figures that matter for working, buying a home, paying bills and retiring in Poland, so you can see them together and see how Poland compares. Each section links to our full guide for that topic, which covers every country and lists the original sources, and each dataset can be downloaded free.

Minimum Wage in Poland (2026)

The legal minimum wage in Poland is €1,119/month. For a month of full-time work that is about $1,252 at current exchange rates, 17th highest of 38 countries in our comparison.

Full table for every country, with sources: Minimum Wage by Country 2026: Hourly and Monthly Rates in US Dollars. Download the data (CSV).

Income Tax and Take-Home Pay in Poland

A single worker on the average wage in Poland (about $54,000 at purchasing-power parity) pays 24.4% of gross pay in income tax and employee social security, so they keep 76%. That is 18th lowest of 38 countries, against an OECD average of 25.1%.

Income tax and employee social security take 24.4% of pay at the average wage, 22.6% at two-thirds of it and 29.3% at 1.67 times it. Including employer contributions, the total tax wedge is 35.0% of labour costs.

Full table for every country, with sources: Income Tax by Country 2026: How Much of Your Salary You Keep in 38 Countries. Download the data (CSV).

Pay Rises in Poland: 2027 Forecast

Employers in Poland expect to raise salaries by 5.0% in 2027 (median of the major pay surveys), after 4.8% in 2026. With inflation at % (), that is roughly flat in real terms.

Full table for every country, with sources: Salary Increase Forecasts 2027 by Country: Every Major Survey in One Table. Download the data (CSV).

Electricity Prices in Poland

Households in Poland pay about €0.300 per kWh of electricity (about $0.34), 8th most expensive of 33 countries; the EU average is €0.283. Change: +10.7% vs late 2025.

Typical household using 2,500–5,000 kWh a year, all taxes included, January–June 2026.

Full table for every country, with sources: Electricity Prices by Country 2026: What Households Pay per kWh, and What the Iran War Means for Bills. Download the data (CSV).

Petrol Prices in Poland Since the Iran War

Petrol in Poland costs €1.56/L (week of 19 October 2026), up 13.3% from €1.38/L in the week before the Iran war began. It peaked at €1.85/L (28 Sep). At about $1.75 a litre it is 3rd cheapest of 29 countries, and the rise is 2nd smallest of 29 countries.

Full table for every country, with sources: Petrol Prices Since the Iran War: How Much They Have Risen in 35 Countries. Download the data (CSV).

Retirement Age in Poland

The state pension age in Poland is 65 men / 60 women for people reaching it in 2026; the earliest you can claim is —. Future change: none legislated. Poland reversed a planned rise to 67 in 2017.

Full table for every country, with sources: Retirement Age by Country 2026: State Pension Ages in 39 Countries. Download the data (CSV).

How Much the State Pension Pays in Poland

A full-career average earner in Poland can expect a mandatory pension worth about 40.6% of their previous net pay, 6th least generous of 50 countries (OECD average 63.2%). Low earner (half the average wage): 41%. High earner (twice the average): 37%.

Full table for every country, with sources: State Pension Amounts by Country 2026: How Much Retirees Actually Get. Download the data (CSV).

How Much of Your Money Is Protected in Poland

Bank deposits in Poland are protected up to €100,000 per depositor, per bank (about $111,900), the limit set by EU law for every member state. Harmonised by EU law; local-currency equivalent outside the euro. Money in payment apps and e-money wallets is usually not covered.

Frequently Asked Questions

The minimum wage in Poland is €1,119/month, about $1,252 a month for full-time work. That is 17th highest of 38 countries.

How much tax do you pay in Poland?

On the average wage, income tax plus employee social security in Poland take 24.4% of gross pay, so a single worker keeps 76% (OECD average: 25.1%).

Pay surveys forecast an average salary increase of 5.0% in Poland for 2027, against inflation of %.

Household electricity in Poland costs about €0.300 per kWh (about $0.34), 8th most expensive of 33 countries.

Petrol in Poland has risen 13.3% since February 2026, from €1.38/L to €1.56/L.

What is the retirement age in Poland?

The state pension age in Poland is 65 men / 60 women in 2026, with the earliest claim at —. Legislated change: None legislated.

In Poland, mandatory pensions replace about 40.6% of an average earner's net pay after a full career, against an OECD average of 63.2%.

Deposits in Poland are insured up to €100,000 per person, per bank.
